title: A faster CI job that cannot hide a failing step
diff:
concurrency:
  group: test-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.npm
          key: npm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            npm-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Install and test
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npm ci
          npm test 2>&1 | tee test.log

concepts.description: A cache key built from a hash of the lockfile changes exactly when the dependencies change, so the cache is reused until it would be wrong.
concepts.context: the actions/cache key in test.yml hashes package-lock.json so a dependency change gets a fresh cache

concepts.description: A restore key matches by prefix, so a near-miss cache still seeds the install when the exact key is absent.
concepts.context: restore-keys in test.yml falls back to the newest npm cache for the same OS

concepts.description: A concurrency group with cancel-in-progress stops superseded runs of the same branch, so only the latest push is tested.
concepts.context: the concurrency block in test.yml cancels an older run when the same ref is pushed again

concepts.description: Without pipefail a pipeline's status is its last command's, so a failing test run piped into tee would be reported as success.
concepts.context: set -euo pipefail in test.yml keeps `npm test | tee test.log` from masking a failing npm test
